steps.title: Cell seeding and growth
steps.instruction: Seed HeLa S3 cells and grow them to the required density before harvesting.

substeps.instruction: Seed 1.0 × 10⁶ cells per 10 cm dish in 10 mL DMEM containing 10 % FBS and penicillin‑streptomycin.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, humidified atmosphere.
When cells reach ~70‑80 % confluency, passage them; a minimum of 2 × 10⁷ cells (≈4 dishes) is needed for downstream cryo‑EM.

steps.title: Cell washing and collection
steps.instruction: Wash, detach, and collect cells while keeping them cold.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate medium and wash cells twice with 5 mL PBS pre‑chilled at 4 °C.
Harvest cells using a cell scraper.
Resuspend the harvested cells in 10 mL cold PBS and transfer to a 15 mL conical tube.
Count cells with an automated counter or hemocytometer.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant with a pipette.
Place the tube on ice.

steps.title: Nuclei isolation and crosslinking
steps.instruction: Isolate nuclei, crosslink chromatin with formaldehyde, and quench the reaction.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in cold CERI buffer (from NE‑PER) to 1.0 × 10⁷ cells · mL⁻¹.
Add protease inhibitor cocktail at 1/100 of the total volume.
Vortex 15 s, then place on ice for 10 min.
Add 55 µL cold CERII buffer per 1 mL sample, vortex 5 s.
Ice 1 min, vortex 5 s.
Centrifuge at 16 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend nuclear pellet in cold PBS to 1.0 × 10⁷ nuclei · mL⁻¹ (based on initial cell number).
Dispense 500 µL (0.5 × 10⁷ nuclei) into individual tubes.
Add formaldehyde to a final concentration of 1 % (v/v) and mix by pipetting/inverting.
Incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Add 2 M glycine to a final concentration of 150 mM and mix.
Incubate 3 min at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 16 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in Buffer A (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 200 mM KCl, 1 mM CaCl₂, 0.5 % NP‑40) to 2.0 × 10⁷ nuclei per 500 µL (4.0 × 10⁷ nuclei · mL⁻¹) and keep on ice.
Dispense 500 µL aliquots of the nuclear suspension into tubes and keep on ice.
Sonicate with a VP‑050N ultrasonic homogenizer (TAITEC) equipped with a 2 mm microtip: PWM = 20 %, 3 s on/7 s off, for 6 cycles.
Return the samples to ice.

steps.title: MNase titration (optimization)
steps.instruction: Determine the optimal MNase amount for chromatin fragmentation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare MNase dilutions in Buffer A to obtain final activities of 200, 40, 8, 1.6, and 0.32 U · µL⁻¹ (serial dilutions).
Aliquot 10 µL of the sonicated sample into five tubes.
Add 0.5 µL of each MNase dilution to the corresponding tube and mix.
Incubate 40 min at 37 °C.
Add 0.5 M EDTA to a final concentration of 10 mM to stop the reaction.
Centrifuge at 16 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and collect the supernatants.
Place tubes on ice.
Treat half of each supernatant with Proteinase K mix (0.5 µL mix to 5 µL sample) and incubate 15 min at 37 °C; keep the other half untreated for direct gel loading.
Add 30 % (w/v) sucrose to reach a final concentration of 5 % (w/v) (e.g., 1 µL 30 % sucrose to 5 µL sample).
Load 20 µL of each preparation onto a 1.5 % agarose gel prepared in 1× TAE.
Run electrophoresis, stain gel in EtBr (0.5 µg · mL⁻¹) for 10 min, destain in Milli‑Q water for 10 min, and image with a UV transilluminator.
Select the MNase concentration that yields the desired nucleosomal DNA pattern in the Proteinase K‑treated lane.

steps.title: Prepare sucrose gradient
steps.instruction: Make a continuous 10 %–50 % (w/v) sucrose gradient for ultracentrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Using a Gradient Master 108, mix 10 % sucrose solution (5 g sucrose + Milli‑Q water to 50 mL) and 50 % sucrose solution (25 g sucrose + Milli‑Q water to 50 mL) each containing 10 mM HEPES‑NaOH pH 7.5, 30 mM NaCl, and 1 mM DTT.
Form the gradient in ultra‑clear tubes (14 × 89 mm) at room temperature.
Chill the prepared gradient at 4 °C before use.

steps.title: MNase digestion and ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Digest chromatin with the chosen MNase amount and separate fragments by density gradient ultracentrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑incubate the remaining sonicated sample 5 min at 37 °C.
Add MNase at the concentration determined in the titration step.
Incubate 40 min at 37 °C.
Add 0.5 M EDTA to a final concentration of 10 mM.
Centrifuge at 16 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and collect the supernatant (~500 µL) without disturbing the pellet.
Layer the fragmented chromatin onto the top of the chilled sucrose gradient.
Ultracentrifuge at ~210 000 × g (35 000 rpm, SW 41 Ti rotor) for 21 h at 4 °C using an Optima XPN‑80.

steps.title: Fraction collection and analysis
steps.instruction: Collect gradient fractions, assess fragment sizes, and pool similar fractions.

substeps.instruction: Collect 660 µL aliquots sequentially from the top of the gradient and keep on ice.
Add Proteinase K mix to each fraction (2 µL mix to 20 µL fraction) and incubate 15 min at 37 °C; for the input sample, add 0.5 µL mix to 5 µL input.
Run 1.5 % agarose gels in 1× TAE, stain with EtBr, destain in water, and image under UV as described above.
Based on the gel, combine fractions that contain DNA fragments of similar length.

steps.title: Buffer exchange and concentration
steps.instruction: Exchange fractions into Buffer B and concentrate the chromatin.

substeps.instruction: Pass the pooled fractions through a pre‑packed PD‑10 column (Cytiva) equilibrated with Buffer B (10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 30 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT).
Concentrate the eluate using an Amicon Ultra‑4 centrifugal filter unit (30 kDa MWCO) to the desired volume.
Measure dsDNA concentration of the final preparation with a NanoDrop One spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Cryo‑EM grid preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare vitrified EM grids from the purified chromatin fragments.

substeps.instruction: Glow‑discharge Quantifoil R1.2/1.3 200‑mesh Cu grids using a PIB‑10 device in soft mode for 2 min.
On a Vitrobot Mark IV set to 4 °C and 100 % humidity, apply 2.5 µL of the chromatin sample to a glow‑discharged grid.
Blot for 4–6 s (wait time = 0 s, blot force = 0, blot total = 1, drain time = 0 s).
Plunge‑freeze the grid into liquid ethane, then mount it in a C‑clip and C‑clip ring.
Store grids in liquid nitrogen.
Acquire micrographs on a Krios G4 cryo‑TEM (300 kV, 81 000× magnification, pixel size 1.06 Å, defocus –2.5 µm, 40 frames over 4.5 s, total dose ≈60 e⁻ · Å⁻²).

description: Validation of protocol This protocol is an optimized version of the chromatin preparation method for cryo-EM analysis previously described in our original research article: Hatazawa et al. [19]. Cryo‐EM structures of native chromatin units from human cells. Genes to Cells (Figures 1–4 and Figure S1).
